items.title: Section: The Meditator Who Mistook Bliss for Nirvāṇa, and Sixty-Two Views Sorted Three Ways

items.zh: 當知此見略有二種。一者、增益，二者、損減。薩迦耶見、邊執見、見取、戒禁取，此四見等，一切皆名增益邪見。謗因、謗用、謗果、壞實事等，心執增益所有諸見，一切皆名損減邪見。無施、無愛，亦無祠祀，是名謗因。無有妙行，亦無惡行，是名謗用。無有妙行、惡行諸業果及異熟，是名謗果。無父無母、無化生有情，亦無世間真阿羅漢諸漏永盡，乃至廣說，如是一切名壞實事。又此邪見，即計前際諸無因論、邊無邊論、不死矯亂論，及計後際現法涅槃等論所有沙門、若婆羅門。當知如是薩迦耶見以為根本六十二見，三見所攝，謂常見所攝諸邊執見、斷見所攝諸邊執見，及諸邪見。
items.en: This view is, in brief, of two kinds: superimposing, and negating. Self-view, extreme view, view-attachment, and attachment to wrong precepts are all called superimposing wrong view. Denying cause, denying function, denying result, and destroying genuine facts are all called negating wrong view. Denying that giving, honouring, or offering accomplish anything is called denying cause. Denying that wholesome or unwholesome conduct does anything is called denying function. Denying that such conduct produces any karmic fruit is called denying result. Denying father, mother, spontaneously born beings, or any genuine arhat in the world who has truly exhausted every affliction, and so on, is called destroying genuine facts. It should be understood that these sixty-two views, rooted in self-view, are subsumed under three categories: extreme view subsumed under the permanence view, extreme view subsumed under the annihilation view, and wrong views themselves.

items.title: Section: Clinging to a View as the Only Truth, and the Deeper Roots of Craving

items.zh: 見取者，於六十二諸見趣等，一一別計為最、為上、為勝、為妙，威勢取執，隨起言說：唯此諦實，餘皆虛妄。由此見故，能得清淨、解脫、出離，是名見取。戒禁取者，謂所受持隨順見取、見取眷屬、見取隨法若戒若禁，於所受持諸戒禁中，妄計為最、為上、為勝、為妙，威勢執取，隨起言說：唯此諦實，餘皆虛妄。由此戒禁，能得清淨、解脫、出離，是名戒禁取。貪者，謂能耽著心所為性。此復四種。謂著諸見、欲、色、無色。
items.en: View-attachment is clinging, one by one, to any of the sixty-two views as the finest, most excellent, most supreme, most sublime, declaring: only this is true, all else is false. Through this view, purity, liberation, and release are believed to be attained — this is view-attachment. Attachment to wrong precepts and observances is clinging to whatever discipline accords with, belongs to, or follows from view-attachment, mistakenly regarding it as the finest, most excellent, most supreme, most sublime, declaring: only this is true, all else is false. Through this discipline, purity, liberation, and release are believed to be attained — this is attachment to wrong precepts. Greed is the mental factor whose nature is to indulge and cling. It is further of four kinds: clinging to views, and to the desire, form, and formless realms.

items.title: Section: Four Faces of Hatred, and the Seven Kinds of Pride Behind Every Comparison

items.zh: 恚者，謂能損害心所為性。此復四種。謂於損己他見、他有情所，及於所愛不饒益所、於所不愛作饒益所所有瞋恚。慢者，謂令心舉心所為性。此復四種。謂於諸見、於諸有情、於受用欲、於諸後有處起。
items.en: Hatred is the mental factor whose nature is to cause harm. It is further of four kinds: hatred towards another's view that has harmed oneself, towards another being who has harmed oneself, towards one who fails to benefit what one loves, and towards one who benefits what one does not love. Conceit is the mental factor whose nature is to make the mind swell. It is further of four kinds, arising in relation to views, to other beings, to enjoyed pleasures, and to future existence.

items.title: Section: Seven Kinds of Pride, and the Difference Between Confidence and Delusion

items.zh: 又此慢略有二種。一、惑亂慢，二、不惑亂慢。於有情處慢者，謂三慢類，已如前說。於受用欲處慢者，謂由大財、大族、大徒眾等現在前故，心遂高舉。於後有處慢者，謂由計我當有不有，廣說乃至我當非想非非想等，若動不動，戲論造作諸愛趣中，現前轉故，心遂高舉。不惑亂慢者，謂於下劣計己為勝、於等計等而生憍慢。惑亂慢者，謂餘六慢。又由受用鄙劣資具，自謂富樂，名惑亂慢。若由受用勝妙資具，自謂富樂，名不惑亂慢。又由邪行，謂後有勝，名惑亂慢。若由正行，謂後有勝，名不惑亂慢。
items.en: This conceit is, in brief, of two kinds: confused conceit, and unconfused conceit. Unconfused conceit is feeling superior to one genuinely inferior, or equal to one genuinely equal. Confused conceit is the remaining six kinds. Also, taking pride in wealth and happiness while using only inferior resources is confused conceit; while using genuinely excellent resources, it is unconfused conceit. Taking pride in a superior future existence through wrongful conduct is confused conceit; through upright conduct, it is unconfused conceit.

items.title: Section: The Ignorance Even an Arhat Still Carries

items.zh: 無明者，謂於所知真實覺悟能覆、能障，心所為性。此略四種。一、無解愚，二、放逸愚，三、染污愚，四、不染污愚。若於不見聞覺知所知義中所有無智，名無解愚。若於見聞覺知所知義中散亂失念所有無智，名放逸愚。於顛倒心所有無智，名染污愚。不顛倒心所有無智，名不染污愚。又此無明總有二種。一、煩惱相應無明，二、獨行無明。非無愚癡而起諸惑，是故貪等餘惑相應所有無明，名煩惱相應無明。若無貪等諸煩惱纏，但於苦等諸諦境中，由不如理作意力故，鈍慧士夫補特伽羅，諸不如實簡擇、覆障、纏裹、闇昧等心所性，名獨行無明。
items.en: Ignorance is the mental factor whose nature is to obscure and obstruct genuine awakening to what is known. It is, in brief, of four kinds: uncomprehending ignorance, negligent ignorance, defiled ignorance, and undefiled ignorance. Not understanding what has never been seen, heard, sensed, or cognized is called uncomprehending ignorance. Losing mindfulness amid distraction, regarding what has been seen, heard, sensed, or cognized, is called negligent ignorance. Confusion bound up with a distorted mind is called defiled ignorance. Confusion without such distortion is called undefiled ignorance. This ignorance is also, altogether, of two kinds: ignorance associated with affliction, and independently arising ignorance.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Doubt, and Closing the Catalogue of Ten Root Afflictions

items.zh: 疑者，猶豫二分不決定，心所為性。當知此疑，略由五相差別建立。謂於他世作用、因、果、諸諦、寶中，心懷猶豫。如是所說十種煩惱，亦緣事轉、亦緣煩惱。
items.en: Doubt is the mental factor whose nature is hesitating, undecided, between two possibilities. It should be understood that this doubt is, in brief, established through five distinguishing aspects: hesitation concerning other lives, function, cause and effect, the truths, and the Three Jewels. These ten afflictions just described take as their object both ordinary phenomena and other afflictions themselves.

items.zh: 謂十煩惱皆與自地一切煩惱展轉相緣，亦緣自地諸有漏事。

blocks.text: The ten root afflictions, defined one by one.

Master Cháng Bǎi: holding as existent what does not exist is superimposition; holding as non-existent what does exist is denial. Thinking the Three Jewels have no merit is one form of wrong view. The sixty-two views all rest on self-view.

Master Cháng Bǎi: view-attachment holds a wrong view to be the most excellent way to release. Precept-attachment takes conduct adopted on such a view as purifying. Greed's nature is to indulge and cling.

Master Cháng Bǎi: if someone fails to help one I love, I feel they harm what is mine; if someone cherishes one I dislike, it feels like opposition. Pride always rests on self-view, comparing oneself with those below, equal, or above.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "confused" pride swells without real grounds; "unconfused" pride swells on qualities one actually has. It is still pride.
"A mental factor that obscures and obstructs." Master Cháng Bǎi: it covers beings so they cannot know that there is no self. Ignorance is not only joined with afflictions; it also arises alone.
Hesitation between two sides. Master Cháng Bǎi: whether a thing is this or that, the mind undecided, is doubt about fact or principle.
"Unconfused pride" is pride in qualities we really have. The treatise still calls it pride. Real qualities do not need defending.

quiz.q: How do superimposing and negating differ, and why is there superimposition in negation?
options: denying what exists is superimposition, adding the thought of absence
superimposing is outsiders'; negating is Buddhist
superimposing concerns wealth; negating concerns lifespan
calling what is not as is superimposes, and the reverse negates; negation first affirms the thing, then denies it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: holding as existent what does not exist is superimposing; holding as nonexistent what does exist is negating; when a negating view arises, the mind first affirms the thing and then denies it. This helps explain why the Chinese says 心執增益 here, which the English leaves out.

quiz.q: Per this fascicle, what is each of the four denials?
options: no parents; no giving; no arhats; no conduct, denying parents being denial of cause, as they are the cause of the body, and denying giving only denial of function
no past life; no next life; no present life; no gods
no suffering; no origin; no cessation; no path
no giving or offering; no good or bad conduct; no fruit or ripening; no parents, spontaneous beings, or arhats
quiz.why: The treatise gives these four. Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking the Three Jewels have no merit and need no offering is one form of the first; denying the ripened and corresponding results of good and bad conduct is denial of result. Other passages classify parents differently, so the answer is limited to this fascicle.

quiz.q: What is the root of the sixty-two views, and under which three are they subsumed?
options: rooted in ignorance; view-attachment, precept-attachment, and wrong view
rooted in self-view; extreme view of permanence, of annihilation, and wrong views
rooted in greed; views of the three realms
rooted in conceit; views of the three times
quiz.why: The treatise roots the sixty-two in self-view and sorts them into three. Master Cháng Bǎi: false speculation about the past gives rise to theories of universal and partial eternity; the view that a person, like a lamp, is extinguished at death is annihilation view.

quiz.q: How does view-attachment differ from wrong view, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: view-attachment is believing another's view and wrong view devising one's own, their content being the same, and so it is lighter and need not be listed separately
view-attachment takes only precepts; wrong view only cause and effect
view-attachment holds wrong views as supreme, the way of final release
view-attachment is a good view; wrong view a bad one
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: view-attachment also clings to wrong views; the difference is that it holds a wrong view to be the most excellent way to final release; since one clings to only these ideas as able to purify and liberate, it is called view-attachment.

quiz.q: What does attachment to precepts and observances grasp?
options: all the Buddha's precepts, since any keeping is attachment
precepts taken in past lives
discipline that accords with, belongs to, or follows view-attachment, as supreme
the community's dietary rules
quiz.why: The treatise limits this to discipline that accords with view-attachment. Master Cháng Bǎi: conduct of guarding body and speech taken up on the basis of view-attachment is falsely reckoned supreme. It does not refer to Buddhist precepts as such. The English "wrong precepts" adds "wrong" to make this clear.

quiz.q: The English has only "clinging" for 威勢取執. What is lost?
options: nothing: 威勢 means outsiders' worldly power, not the grasping itself, and is rightly omitted for flow, the text not repeating it later
it omits 威勢: the lecture speaks of forceful grasping, and the precept passage has the same omission
it omits 取, and should read "mighty"
it omits the sixty-two views
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one regards each view as most excellent and grasps it with great force. 威勢 describes the force of the grasping, and the same phrase comes back under precept-attachment. The English "clinging" in both places drops this forcefulness.

quiz.q: What is greed's nature and its four kinds?
options: causing harm; wealth, sex, fame, and food
swelling the mind; views, beings, pleasures, future existence
obscuring awakening; the four truths
indulging and clinging; to views, and the desire, form, and formless realms
quiz.why: The treatise defines greed as the factor whose nature is to indulge and cling. Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind is immersed and stained in lovely objects, the inner body and outer forms and sounds. Note that greed for views stands alongside greed for the three realms.

quiz.q: The English has "towards failure to benefit what one loves." What is wrong with the object?
options: no problem: hatred's object is the event, not the person, 所 meaning a place or matter, and "failure" shows this, as in the lecture
所 is the person: hatred's object is a being, while the English aims it at the failure itself
the problem is "benefit," which should be "profit"
the problem is "loves," which should be "owns"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: towards another who does not benefit the one I love, I feel it harms what is mine; if another cherishes someone I dislike, it feels like opposing me. In both, hatred falls on the other person. The English makes the object an event, failing to show this.

quiz.q: What does conceit rest on, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain conceit about future existence?
options: it rests on greed; the future case is fear of evil destinies
it rests on self-view, in comparing oneself; one also swells over expected human or divine results
it rests on faith; one swells over the Dharma
it rests on ignorance; one swells over past lives
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: conceit always rests on self-view; comparing oneself with those inferior, equal, or superior gives rise to many kinds of conceit; regarding the lovely results of humans and gods in the next life, one's mind also swells. The English "swell" is apt for 舉.

quiz.q: How do confused and unconfused conceit differ?
options: confused: superior to the inferior, equal to the equal; unconfused: the other six, thinking oneself better being the confusion, the rest having a factual basis
confused is of the desire realm; unconfused of the higher ones
unconfused: superior to the inferior, equal to the equal; confused: the other six
confused is severed by vision; unconfused by cultivation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: confused means a mistaken self-assessment, swelling without excellent conditions; unconfused means swelling from excellent conditions one actually has. It is still conceit, as the treatise says 而生憍慢, even when the comparison is accurate.

quiz.q: What common problem does Master Cháng Bǎi find in pride over poor resources and wrongful conduct?
options: both are envy: unable to bear others' fine resources or right conduct
both are annihilation view, denying a next life
they do not fit the facts: thinking the poor noble, and expecting a fine rebirth from distorted conduct
both are wholesome, fostering contentment
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: using coarse, poor resources yet thinking oneself noble and rich is conceit that does not fit the facts; committing distorted deeds and yet thinking the next life's result will be excellent is the same. The English "taking pride" is clear here.

quiz.q: What is the nature of ignorance?
options: the factor that obscures and obstructs genuine awakening to what is known
a state with no mental activity at all, not a factor but merely wisdom's absence, as darkness is light's absence, given no nature of its own in the treatise
the factor of hesitating between two possibilities
the factor that swells the mind
quiz.why: The treatise calls it a mental factor that obscures and obstructs. Master Cháng Bǎi: a factor covering beings, so that they cannot know the fact and truth of no-self and nothing belonging to self in all phenomena. It is a positive factor, not a mere absence of knowledge.

quiz.q: How do uncomprehending and negligent ignorance differ, and what examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: hearing and rejecting the Dharma is the first; never hearing it the second
the first is an affliction; the second is not
never having contemplated no-self is the first; losing mindfulness amid distraction is the second
the first is of the higher realms; the second of the desire realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for instance, not having contemplated the aggregates as no-self, one cannot enter reality, and has uncomprehending ignorance about the aggregates; through distraction and lost mindfulness, often forgetting right mindfulness and wisdom, one has negligent ignorance.

quiz.q: How do defiled and undefiled ignorance differ, and what are ignorance's two overall kinds?
options: with wholesome or unwholesome mind, the former being undefiled; overall divided into ignorance severed by vision and by cultivation
in the desire or higher realms; innate and adopted
lack of knowledge with a distorted or undistorted mind; associated and independent
about past or future; with and without substance
quiz.why: The treatise divides by distorted and undistorted mind, and then into ignorance associated with affliction and independent ignorance. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not the case that afflictions arise without delusion. The English "independently arising ignorance" renders 獨行 well.

quiz.q: What is the nature of doubt?
options: the factor of hesitating, undecided, between two possibilities
the factor of wholly disbelieving the Three Jewels
the factor of failing to awaken to reality
the factor of lowering the mind
quiz.why: The treatise defines doubt as hesitation between two sides. Master Cháng Bǎi: whether a thing is this or that, the mind undecided on two sides, is doubt, about matter or principle. Doubt remains undecided, which separates it from the firm denial of wrong view.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "take as object both phenomena and afflictions"?
options: afflictions take only outer things, not afflictions, and so the phrase only means objects cause them, inner greed never being another affliction's object
at times they appear taking the mind's own discriminated afflictions as object
only ignorance can take affliction
only higher afflictions can take lower ones
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: sometimes they appear taking the mind's own discriminated afflictions as object, and so it is said they turn on matters and also on afflictions. For example, one can feel conceit about one's own views or hatred of one's own greed. The English is correct.
